title: Research apprenticeship and qualifying exams
stage: Graduate study and research in neuroscience
audience: a graduate preparing for research in neuroscience or cognitive science, or a graduate student in the first years of a PhD or a research role
purpose: Complete the first milestones of a research career in neuroscience or cognitive science: reanalyze or reproduce a published result from open data and extend it, write it up as a short paper and present it, prepare for qualifying exams that span cellular, systems, cognitive and computational neuroscience and methods, and choose a thesis direction, an advisor and the next steps toward a PhD or a research role.
primary_reading: OpenNeuro, a free archive of open neuroimaging data sets

weeks.1: Choosing a result to reproduce from open data
weeks.2: Planning a reanalysis: scope, data and success criteria
weeks.4: When results do not match: debugging and honest reporting
weeks.5: Extending a result: new analyses and controls
weeks.7: Qualifying exam review: cellular and systems neuroscience
weeks.8: Qualifying exam review: cognitive and computational neuroscience
weeks.9: Qualifying exam review: methods, statistics and ethics
weeks.11: Choosing a thesis direction and an advisor
weeks.12: Paths in research: PhD programs, research jobs and other routes

blocks.deliverable: Report your first results with their uncertainty.
Draft the paper's methods and results sections.
Week 7 midterm; answer timed questions across the field.
Take a mock oral exam on your reading list.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Reanalysis paper: reproduce one published result from an open neuroscience or psychology data set with modest computing, extend it with one new analysis or control, write a four- to six-page paper that reports honestly what did and did not reproduce, share your code with instructions, and pass a mock qualifying exam of three timed answers.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
